c.tagline: Cantonese trade hub of dim sum and towers.

emergency.note: Fire is 119; English-speaking operators are rare, so have a Chinese speaker or hotel staff call.

hood_landmark.Tianhe: Zhujiang New Town's skyscraper skyline and the Guangzhou Opera House
hood_landmark.Yuexiu: Yuexiu Park with the Five Rams Statue and Zhenhai Tower
hood_landmark.Haizhu: The 600m Canton Tower on the Pearl River
hood_landmark.Panyu: Chimelong resort's safari park and amusement rides

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around the railway station and crowded markets

hood_desc: Tianhe is the modern central business district packed with skyscrapers, luxury malls along Tianhe Road, and nightlife; it suits business travelers, shoppers, and those wanting a polished urban base.
Yuexiu is the historic old city core with temples, colonial architecture, parks, and government offices; it suits first-time visitors and history lovers who want central, walkable heritage sights.
Liwan is the heart of traditional Cantonese culture with Xiguan lanes, Shamian Island, and famous dim sum; it suits foodies and travelers seeking old-world local atmosphere.
Haizhu is a leafy island district south of the Pearl River near Canton Tower, with parks and residential calm; it suits families and travelers wanting riverside views at mid-range prices.
Panyu is a spread-out southern suburban district home to Chimelong theme parks and resorts; it suits families and budget-minded visitors who do not mind being farther from downtown.
lodging: Holiday Inn Express Guangzhou Exhibition Center

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or boiled water, which is the local norm even for residents.

transit.pay: Use a Yang Cheng Tong transit card (metro, buses and ferries), scan a QR code in the Guangzhou Metro app or Alipay/WeChat Pay, or tap a Visa, Mastercard or UnionPay contactless bank card at the gate. Cards and tickets are sold from vending machines and staffed windows in every station. A single ride starts at ¥2 (about $0.30) and rises with distance to about ¥20 (~$2.80); a 24-hour unlimited pass is also ¥20.
transit.hours: Most metro lines run daily from around 6am until 11pm-midnight, with no overnight metro; a handful of night-bus routes cover major corridors after the metro closes.

transit.m: Guangzhou Metro Line 3 to Tianhe CBD, 30-40 min
Airport Express Bus to downtown, 50-90 min

food.name: Dim sum (morning tea)
food.desc: Yum cha in its birthplace: har gow, siu mai, char siu bao and chicken feet with tea, from carts and bamboo steamers in century-old halls.

places.name: Dian Dou De
places.note: Michelin Bib Gourmand chain serving all-day dim sum; locals' most-named pick

places.name: Tao Tao Ju
places.note: Open since 1880 and Michelin-listed; har gow and char siu bao are benchmarks

food.name: Rice noodle rolls (changfen)
food.desc: Silky steamed rice sheets rolled around beef, shrimp or egg, doused in sweet soy - the classic Cantonese breakfast.

places.name: Yin Ji Cheong Fun
places.note: Founded 1958; its smooth signature rolls are the city's reference point

places.name: Fang Ji Snack Shop
places.note: Old-school snack shop named in recent local changfen roundups

food.name: Wonton noodles
food.desc: Springy bamboo-pressed egg noodles with shrimp-pork wontons in a light broth - perfected over decades in Xiguan's noodle houses.

places.name: Wu Cai Ji (Wu Choi Kee)
places.note: Michelin-recommended five years running; 70-year-old family noodle house

places.name: Bao Hua Noodle Shop
places.note: Old-school Xiguan wonton noodle stop beloved by locals

food.name: Claypot rice (bao zai fan)
food.desc: Rice crisped in a clay pot under cured sausage, chicken or eel, finished with sweet soy - the crusty bottom layer is the prize.

places.name: Min Ji Claypot Rice
places.note: Repeatedly named the city's must-try claypot specialist in 2025 food guides

places.name: Wan Xing Xiao Shi
places.note: Casual eatery on local best-claypot lists; go at night like locals

food.name: White cut chicken
food.desc: Poached free-range chicken served at room temperature with ginger-scallion oil - simplicity that shows off Cantonese technique.

places.name: Qingping Restaurant
places.note: Historic home of Qingping chicken, the city's most famous white cut style

places.name: Tao Tao Ju
places.note: Century-old hall where white cut chicken anchors the Cantonese menu

food.name: Tong sui sweet soups
food.desc: Cantonese 'sugar water' desserts - double-skin milk, black sesame paste and red bean soups served warm or chilled after dinner.

places.name: Nan Xin Milk Desserts
places.note: Famous since the 1930s for shuang pi nai, the wobbly double-skin milk custard

places.name: Bai Hua Dessert
places.note: Local-favorite canteen with dozens of classic sweet soups

food.name: Herbal tea (liangcha)
food.desc: Bitter 'cooling teas' brewed from Lingnan herbs, sold by the bowl at storefront counters - Guangzhou's traditional cure-all.

places.name: Huang Zhen Long
places.note: Century-old herbal tea brand; order the classic bitter 24-herb brew

places.name: Ping An Tang
places.note: Popular local liangcha chain for a quick bowl on a hot day

food.name: Zhujiang (Pearl River) beer
food.desc: Guangzhou's own lager, brewed beside the Pearl River since 1985 - best drunk cold with seafood or at the riverside beer zone.

places.name: Party Pier Beer Culture Zone
places.note: Bar-and-taproom strip at the original Zhujiang brewery site, lively at night

places.name: The Happy Monk
places.note: Popular beer bar pouring Zhujiang alongside local craft taps

landmarks: Canton Tower
A soaring 600-meter twisting steel tower that dominates the skyline over the Pearl River, especially striking when lit up at night.
Temple of the Six Banyan Trees
A working Buddhist temple famous for its ornate Flower Pagoda, one of Guangzhou's oldest and most photogenic religious structures.
Chen Clan Ancestral Hall
An exquisitely decorated 19th-century ancestral hall showcasing intricate Lingnan wood, stone, and ceramic carvings.
Sacred Heart Cathedral (Shishi Cathedral)
A Gothic-revival granite cathedral built entirely of stone, nicknamed 'Stone House,' unique among China's churches.
Guangzhou Opera House
A futuristic Zaha Hadid-designed building resembling two river-worn boulders, a striking piece of modern architecture on the waterfront.
Chimelong Paradise
One of China's largest theme parks, known for record-breaking rides and vibrant, colorful attractions.
Shamian Island
A leafy former colonial concession island lined with well-preserved European-style buildings and banyan-tree avenues.
Huaisheng Mosque
One of the oldest mosques in the world, notable for its plain white minaret known as the 'Light Tower.'
Guangzhou Circle
A distinctive donut-shaped skyscraper on the Pearl River whose reflection forms a giant '0' — one of the city's most photographed modern buildings.
Guangzhou International Finance Center
A sleek supertall skyscraper (part of the 'Little Manhattan' cluster) offering some of the best skyline views in the city.

intl.to: Hong Kong West Kowloon (Hong Kong SAR)
intl.op: China Railway / MTR High Speed Rail

train.note: Cross-border high-speed trains to Hong Kong West Kowloon leave from Guangzhou South and Guangzhou East (Guangzhou Baiyun also runs some services) - it is a full immigration crossing, so bring your passport and any permit/visa you need. Domestic high-speed trains from Guangzhou South, East and North reach most of China; book on the official 12306 site or app with your passport, or through Trip.com if you want an English interface. Seats on the Hong Kong runs and the Wuhan/Beijing corridor sell out fast around public holidays.

bus.note: Cross-border coaches to Hong Kong and Macau pick up at hotels and terminals around the city and require your passport and any needed permit at the boundary, where everyone gets off the bus to clear immigration; allow 3.5-4 hours to central Hong Kong. Long-distance domestic buses leave from terminals such as the Guangzhou (Provincial) Bus Terminal beside Guangzhou railway station, but for most trips within Guangdong the high-speed train is faster.

intl.to: Hong Kong (HK-Macau Ferry Terminal / airport SkyPier) and Macau

ferry.note: CKS high-speed ferries to Hong Kong and Macau depart from Nansha Port, well south of central Guangzhou, so allow at least an hour and a half to reach it from the city. Crossings take roughly 70-90 minutes and the SkyPier service lets you transfer straight to a flight at Hong Kong airport without clearing HK immigration. Passport and any required permit are needed, and sailings are cut in bad weather or when a typhoon signal is raised.

half.name: Foshan
half.blurb: Neighboring city famed for ancestral temples, martial-arts heritage, and the towering statue atop Mount Xiqiao.

half.name: Kaiping Diaolou
half.blurb: UNESCO-listed fortified watchtowers rise dramatically over quiet villages blending Chinese and Western architectural styles.

half.name: Danxia Mountain
half.blurb: Glowing red sandstone cliffs and peaks form a UNESCO geopark laced with scenic hiking trails.

half.name: Shenzhen
half.blurb: Fast-growing tech metropolis offering theme parks, gardens, and buzzing shopping just a quick train ride away.

half.name: Hong Kong
half.blurb: Dazzling harbor city reached by high-speed rail, mixing skyline views, markets, and green island escapes.

half.name: Zhaoqing
half.blurb: Home to the limestone Seven Star Crags rising from tranquil lakes, ringed by paths and pavilions.
